characters.name: DAVE
characters.description: A regular guy trying to cancel his cable subscription. Wears a tired expression and sweatpants.

characters.name: ZALGOR
characters.description: A demonic entity working as a Tier 1 Support Rep for Comcast/Hell. Wears a headset over his horns.

scenes.visuals: Split screen. Left side: Dave is on his couch in a messy apartment. Right side: Zalgor is in a drab cubicle surrounded by actual hellfire and tormented souls.
audio_cues: Music: Elevator muzak playing faintly in Hell

dialogue.speaker: DAVE
dialogue.text: Yes, I just want to cancel my cable.

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: I can help with that. But first, let me offer you our premium damnation package. It comes with HBO.

dialogue.speaker: DAVE
dialogue.text: I literally only watch YouTube shorts of guys building mud huts. Cancel it.

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: To verify your identity, please recite the screams of your ancestors.

dialogue.speaker: DAVE
dialogue.text: Uh... 'Ahhh?'

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: Incorrect. That was the scream of a mildly inconvenienced barista. Your account is now cursed.

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: Please hold while I transfer you to the abyss.

jokes.description: Hook premise: Canceling cable is literally dealing with a demon from hell.
Damnation package includes HBO.
Dave admits to only watching mud hut videos instead of premium TV.
Verification question is reciting ancestral screams.
Dave's weak, pathetic attempt at a scream.
Demon identifies the scream as a barista's, curses the account.
CUTAWAY: A hipster barista in an apron drops a portafilter and screams 'Ahhh?' exactly like Dave.
The hold music in Hell is a crypto podcast.
Visual gag of Dave extreme aging on hold.
Demon casually eating a human bone like a breakroom snack.

scenes.visuals: Back to split screen. Dave looks older.
audio_cues: SFX: Bear roar in the distance

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: Okay, I can waive the cancellation fee if you solve this riddle.

dialogue.speaker: DAVE
dialogue.text: Is the riddle 'Why is Comcast so terrible?'

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: No, that's not a riddle, that's a business model.

dialogue.speaker: DAVE
dialogue.text: Just cancel it! I'm moving to the woods! I'm going off the grid!

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: Woods are not in our service area, but we can bill you for roaming bear attacks.

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: Would you like to upgrade your router? The new one doesn't smell like burning hair.

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: Smoking kills, which is great for our Q3 quota.

jokes.description: Demon offers riddle instead of simple cancellation.
Dave complains about Comcast.
Demon confirms terrible service is their actual business model.
Dave threatens to live off the grid.
Demon offers to bill him for roaming bear attacks.
CUTAWAY: A large grizzly bear wearing a Comcast badge is shaking down a camper.
Demon offers router upgrade that just doesn't smell bad.
Visual gag: Router is literally on fire in the background.
Dave casually leans over and uses the burning router to light a cigarette.
Hell's quota relies on smoking deaths.

scenes.visuals: Dave is sweating, rubbing his temples. Zalgor is filing his nails with a small pitchfork.

dialogue.speaker: DAVE
dialogue.text: Look, Zalgor, buddy. What do I have to do? Blood sacrifice? Firstborn child?

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: We stopped doing blood sacrifices in '98. Too messy. HR hated it. We just need a verbal agreement.

dialogue.speaker: DAVE
dialogue.text: Okay, I verbally agree to cancel.

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: No, to the terms and conditions. The ones you didn't read in 2014 when you clicked 'Accept'.

dialogue.speaker: DAVE
dialogue.text: Fine! I agree! Whatever it is, I agree! Take everything!

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: Excellent. Your soul is now legally property of the cable company. And your service is... wait for it...

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: Cancelled.

dialogue.speaker: DAVE
dialogue.text: Finally! ...Wait, my soul?

dialogue.speaker: ZALGOR
dialogue.text: Yep. The retention department will collect it on Tuesday between 8 AM and Never. Have a hellish day!

jokes.description: Dave casually offers blood sacrifice out of desperation.
Demon says blood sacrifices are outdated 90s HR policy.
Dave tries simple logic on a demon.
Demon brings up the unread T&Cs from a decade ago.
Dave blindly agrees to terms and conditions, the classic fatal mistake.
Soul becomes property of the cable company.
Demon dramatically pauses for 5 seconds before saying cancelled, making Dave sweat.
Dave's delayed realization of the soul clause.
Punchline Payoff: The classic terrible cable company appointment window applied to soul collection ('between 8 AM and Never').
Final sendoff 'Have a hellish day' as the call drops with a fiery click.
